key_insight: The paper replaces sample-wise RL rewards with distribution-wise rewards to reduce reward hacking, improve diversity, and better align generated images with the target data distribution.
engineering_relevance: For visual generative model finetuning, this offers a more stable RL objective that can improve image quality without collapsing sample diversity, making deployment-friendly post-training optimization more reliable.
method: Evaluate rewards over a generated subset as a distribution, not per image
Use a subset-replace strategy to update only a small part of the reference set for efficiency
Apply RL to optimize post-hoc model merging coefficients to reduce train-inference inconsistency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong FID-50K gains, improving SiT from 8.30 to 5.77 and EDM2 from 3.74 to 3.52, with qualitative results showing better perceptual quality and preserved diversity.
watch_item: Distribution-wise reward estimation and subset management still add algorithmic complexity, so efficiency and stability depend on careful implementation and reward design.
paper_title: Optimizing Visual Generative Models via Distribution-wise Rewards
